fullPassage: An objectively obtained probability is not a guarantee. Although in the long run, we expect a coin to come up heads half the time, probability is not a self-correcting process. The coin has no memory, knowledge, willpower, or volition. There is not some overlord of the theory of probability making sure that everything works out just the way you expect. If you get "heads" ten times in a row, the probability of the coin coming up "tails" on the next toss is still 50%. Tails is not more likely and it is not "due." The notion that chance processes correct themselves is part of the gambler's fallacy, and it has made many casino owners, including Steve Wynn, very wealthy. Millions of people have continued to put money into slot machines under the illusion that their payout is due. It's true that probabilities tend to even out, but only in the long run. And that long run can take more time and money than anyone has.

det.tip: objectively(객관적으로) ↔ subjectively(주관적으로)

questions.passage:
(A) In the long <u>run</u>, patience and steady effort will surely pay off.

(B) Every morning she likes to <u>run</u> along the river to stay healthy.
questions.stem: 다음 밑줄 친 (A)와 (B)의 run의 문맥적 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) in the long run = 장기적으로(기간) / (B) run = 달리다(동사)
det.analysis:
❌ ① 달리다 — (장기적) 기간: (A)와 (B)가 뒤바뀜
❌ ② 경주 — 달리다: (A)의 run은 '경주'가 아니라 '기간'
✅ ③ (장기적) 기간 — 달리다: (A) in the long run은 '장기적으로(기간)', (B) run along the river는 '달리다' ←정답
❌ ④ (장기적) 기간 — 운영하다: (B)는 '운영하다'가 아니라 '달리다'
det.tip: run: in the long run(장기적으로, 기간) vs run(달리다) — 문맥으로 구별

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "a false or mistaken belief, especially one based on unsound reasoning"

det.korean: 잘못된 추론에 근거한 거짓 믿음 → fallacy(오류, 그릇된 생각)
det.analysis:
✅ ① fallacy(오류) — 잘못된 추론에 기반한 그릇된 믿음 ←정답
❌ ② evidence(증거) — 정의와 반대: 근거가 되는 사실
❌ ③ tradition(전통) — 정의와 무관
❌ ④ instinct(본능) — 정의와 무관
det.tip: fallacy = 잘못된 추론에 근거한 오류 (gambler's fallacy = 도박사의 오류)

questions.passage: If you get "heads" ten times in a row, the probability of the coin __________ (come) up "tails" on the next toss is still 50%. Tails is not more likely and it is not "due."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로, 1단어)

det.korean: 명사 the coin 뒤에서 '동전이 ~하는'을 나타내는 동명사/현재분사 자리이므로 come을 coming으로 바꾼다.
det.analysis: the probability of the coin __________ up "tails" → 「of + 명사(the coin) + V-ing」 동명사 구문으로 '동전이 tails가 나올 확률'을 뜻함 → come을 coming으로
det.tip: the probability of the coin coming up = 동전이 ~가 나올 확률 (동명사 coming)

questions.passage: Millions of people have __________ (continue) to put money into slot machines under the illusion that their payout is due. It's true that probabilities tend to even out, but only in the long run.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로, 1단어)

det.korean: have 뒤에서 현재완료를 만드는 자리이므로 continue를 과거분사 continued로 바꾼다.
det.analysis: Millions of people have __________ to put money → 「have + 과거분사」 현재완료(계속 ~해 왔다) → continue를 continued로
det.tip: have continued to ~ = 계속 ~해 왔다 (현재완료 have + p.p.)

questions.passage: An objectively obtained probability is not a guarantee. Although in the long run, we expect a coin to come up heads half the time, probability is not a self-correcting process. The coin has no memory, knowledge, willpower, or volition. There is not some overlord of the theory of probability making sure that everything works out just the way you expect. If you get "heads" ten times in a row, the probability of the coin coming up "tails" on the next toss is still 50%. Tails is not more likely and it is not "due." The notion that __________ is part of the gambler's fallacy, and it has made many casino owners, including Steve Wynn, very wealthy. Millions of people have continued to put money into slot machines under the illusion that their payout is due. It's true that probabilities tend to even out, but only in the long run. And that long run can take more time and money than anyone has.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: '우연의 과정이 스스로를 교정한다'는 관념이 바로 도박사의 오류라는 흐름이다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① every coin toss is truly random(모든 동전 던지기는 순전히 무작위다) — 이는 오히려 옳은 사실이라 '오류'가 될 수 없음
✅ ② chance processes correct themselves(우연의 과정이 스스로 교정된다) — 이 잘못된 관념이 도박사의 오류의 핵심 ←정답
❌ ③ casinos always win in the end(카지노는 결국 항상 이긴다) — 본문에 없는 내용
❌ ④ luck favors the patient player(행운은 참을성 있는 자를 돕는다) — 본문에 없는 내용
det.tip: gambler's fallacy = 우연이 스스로 균형을 맞춘다는 잘못된 관념

ch: every coin toss is truly random
casinos always win in the end

questions.passage: An objectively obtained probability is not a guarantee. Although in the long run, we expect a coin to come up heads half the time, probability is not a self-correcting process. The coin has no memory, knowledge, willpower, or volition. There is not some overlord of the theory of probability making sure that everything works out just the way you expect. If you get "heads" ten times in a row, the probability of the coin coming up "tails" on the next toss is still 50%. Tails is not more likely and it is not "due." The notion that chance processes correct themselves is part of the gambler's fallacy, and it has made many casino owners, including Steve Wynn, very wealthy. Millions of people have continued to put money into slot machines under the illusion that __________. It's true that probabilities tend to even out, but only in the long run. And that long run can take more time and money than anyone has.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 사람들이 '자신의 배당금이 도래했다(이제 나올 때가 됐다)'는 착각 속에서 계속 돈을 넣는다는 흐름이다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① the odds are truly in their favor(승산이 자기편이다) — 본문의 논지(승산은 그대로)와 어긋남
❌ ② they will surely lose everything(모든 것을 잃을 것이다) — 착각의 내용은 손실이 아니라 배당 기대
✅ ③ their payout is due(자신의 배당금이 도래했다) — 이제 딸 때가 됐다는 헛된 믿음 ←정답
❌ ④ the casino owners are cheating(카지노가 속임수를 쓴다) — 본문에 없는 내용
det.tip: the illusion that their payout is due = 이제 배당금(당첨)이 나올 때가 됐다는 착각

ch: the odds are truly in their favor
